### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via writeWallVerdict (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 37 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03de83bfe145eea8f495bcbc9886105715721b3f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c275a36b86cd1c7d4132d4ed4766ab939db676d3` — the merge of head `a3088d01d2a9389bd8b510aa3187f67170e23cdd` into base `03de83bfe145eea8f495bcbc9886105715721b3f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c275a36b86cd1c7d4132d4ed4766ab939db676d3 && git checkout c275a36b86cd1c7d4132d4ed4766ab939db676d3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 03de83bfe145eea8f495bcbc9886105715721b3f a3088d01d2a9389bd8b510aa3187f67170e23cdd && git checkout -B drift-repro 03de83bfe145eea8f495bcbc9886105715721b3f && git merge --no-ff a3088d01d2a9389bd8b510aa3187f67170e23cdd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03de83bfe145eea8f495bcbc9886105715721b3f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 03de83bfe145eea8f495bcbc9886105715721b3f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `0cc6f290aba06b57eec8b0104c7f54902c527409`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/validate-write-wall-verdict.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert-wall-judged-organization.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/write-wall-verdict-equivalence.test.ts, packages/plugins/organizations/src/validate-preview-wall-verdict.test.ts, packages/rest/src/import-dryrun-tenant-wall-parity.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin.ts.json, .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml. The two changesets are judged under ②; `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 6c is checked for truth against the diff under ③. `reviewFace` over the PR's file list returns no schema or governed hit (the paths decide no face; the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line alone would owe `TIER_DEFAULT`); the tier served is the one ruling 6336640643 sets for this delivery, a new published seam on the tenant write wall, and the floor is the whole diff outside the prose faces.

Judged against ruling 6336640643 (letter A, confirmed 6336790186), card #25062 and its comments, the PR body with its Acceptance notes, the dev report 6341141274, and the net diff against the merge base `2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af` (7 commits on the branch; the two measurement-probe commits are reverted by `941fa4e18`, so the net diff holds no probe). Read-only: no checkout, build, test or gate run.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Premise — one method, no second spelling: RIGHT.** At head, step 3.7's judgement is composed by `SecurityPlugin.composeWriteTenantWall` (security-plugin.ts:8333) and the middleware itself calls it at :4110, under the step's unchanged guard (:4091–4096: insert or update, an object payload, a user id). `tenantParts` is declared once (:8461, assigned :8486) and `clearsWall` once (:8488); every other occurrence of either name at head is a comment or inside that method (`judgePayload` :8584, `judgeRow` :8631). The payload half (`wall.preTest ?? wall.judgePayload(writeRows)`) and the stored-image seam (`wall.storedImage.judgeLanding` / `judgeRow` / `judgesOrganization`) both read the composed wall. The three helpers the wall is derived from — `organizationWallRefusal`, `computeWriteTenantWall`, `computeWriteTenantCheckFilter` — are byte-identical between base and head, and the body of `canWriteObject` (the probe's answer) is byte-identical too; only its docblock moved. Engine side: the added lines of engine.ts mention `posture`, `tenantId` and `accessible_org_ids` only inside comments that forbid reading them; `validate()` reads the verdict value (`wallRefusalOf`, `wallJudgesOrganizationOf`, engine.ts:15877–15883) and nothing else. The `OperationContext` interface is untouched by the diff.

Behaviour preservation of the moved step, read condition by condition: parts computed when `writeRows.some(namesOrganization) || this.orgScopingEnabled` (was `suppliedRows.length > 0 || …`, the same set); the forge guard and the emptied-organization refusal gated on `walled` (`tenantParts.length > 0`) as before; the seam installed on `(walled || operatorInsertLacksActiveOrganization) && (insert || singlePayload)` with `singlePayload = !Array.isArray(opCtx.data)`, the base condition verbatim; `judgesOrganization: walled && (insert || (update && singlePayload))`, verbatim; `evaluate` order unchanged (operator landing arm, then the #24784 member arm, then the business check, then the per-row loop); each refusal still warns then throws (`raiseWriteWallRefusal`, :8674) with the base's log line and message text moved whole. The only mechanical difference is that the pre-test's `PermissionDeniedError` is now constructed at compose time rather than at the throw, which changes no code, status or message. The ADR-0123 anchor's ordering invariant (pre-test ahead of the forge guard) holds in both callers: `preTest ?? judgePayload` in the middleware, `preTest ?? judgePayload ?? judgeLanding` in `writeWallVerdict` (:8745).

**(b) Security direction: RIGHT, fail-closed on every exit.** The write path's only change is the extraction above, with equal predicates, so the write admits nothing it refused before. The preview changes in two places only: it spares `organization_id` from the static-`readonly` strip where the verdict says `judgesOrganization` (through `insertStaticReadonlySubject` / `updateStaticReadonlySubject`, engine.ts:2473 / :2500 — the write's own functions, which fall back to the base subject when the flag is false, so an unregistered or `null` verdict reproduces the base strip exactly), and it refuses rows the wall refuses. Neither can make a row preview `valid` where it previewed invalid before: the preview's accept set only shrinks (the refusal), and the drop it stops reporting is one the write does not take. Exits: nothing registered or a `null` answer → today's strip (ruling item 3, pinned UNREGISTERED and NULL); the seam throws → `validate()` rejects — `askWriteWall` (:15864) has no catch, unlike the probe's `.catch(() => false)` at :16136 — pinned ("a verdict that throws rejects the preview"); a wrong-length answer → throws (:15867). Insert vs update: on update the preview's rows are the caller's payload with its address; `judgePayload` judges a supplied or emptied `organization_id`, `judgeLanding` is insert-only, and the stored-image `judgeRow` is not asked — right, because a by-id payload that leaves the column alone keeps the organization the row was selected under. `writeWallVerdict` passes `singlePayload: true` for every row: right for the preview's rows, which the import commits one `update()` per row, and the equivalence pin's update cases are by-id single-row cases. The `null` exits of `writeWallVerdict` (:8724–8731: a system context, no user id, a caller the context prologue refuses) hand the preview its pre-PR answer for callers the write refuses before its wall — a limit that predates this PR and is not widened by it (the preview ran none of the write's caller gates before either). Observation, not a verdict item, carried to the end.

**(c) Prohibitions: KEPT.** The probe's boolean is untouched (body byte-identical; `registerWriteGateProbe` at engine.ts:6336 unchanged; only its docblock corrected). No `OperationContext` member is added (the interface at :3728 is not in the diff; the plugin registers through a feature-detected engine method, :1978). No ride of the middleware chain (`validate()` still calls no `executeWithMiddleware`). No contract text moves (no `packages/spec` path in the file list; `ValidateDataResponseSchema` / `ValidateDataIssueSchema` unchanged).

**(d) Deviation 3, the second ask on the stripped row: INSIDE the ruling, and RIGHT.** The ruling fixes the seam's signature, that `validate()` reads the verdict per row and nothing else, and the limit "after the defaults, before any hook". The second ask (engine.ts:15973–15977) asks the same seam, about the same row as the strips leave it — still before any hook — and reads only the verdict; it writes `wallRefusals[i]` only for a row with no refusal, so it can add a refusal and can never clear one or re-decide the spare. It cannot refuse on the payload half what the first ask admitted: the strips only remove keys, so `namesOrganization` can only go from true to false and an own-property `null` / `''` cannot appear. What it reaches is the #24821 arm the ruling names: a crossing operator with no active organization naming an organization — first ask admitted with `judgesOrganization: false` (no parts), the strip takes the column, the stripped row has nowhere to land, `judgeLanding` refuses `_record` with the write's message. The write does the same on its stored image. Pinned three ways: the engine contract ("ASKED AGAIN … and only about that row"), in process (`[#24821]` case: write 403, preview `_record`, same message), and the equivalence table ("crossing operator with no active organization, a row naming one" admitted on the payload half, as the write's payload half admits it).

**(e) Exported surface: RIGHT in kind; the PR body's one-line parenthetical under-names it.** The diff publishes: `ObjectQL.registerWriteWallVerdict(fn)` (a new public method on an exported class), the types `WriteWallVerdict` and `WriteWallRowVerdict` (added to the `export type` line of `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), and `SecurityPlugin.writeWallVerdict(object, operation, context, rows)` (a new public method on `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s exported `SecurityPlugin`; not a member of `ISecurityService`, no spec change). All additive and optional: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is the right arm on both packages. The objectql changeset names the member and both types; the plugin-security changeset names `writeWallVerdict` as new. The PR body's single `Clause-②` parenthetical ("one additive registration member on @objectstack/objectql's plugin-facing API") names the objectql member only — the plugin-security method is published surface too. The declaration line itself is well-formed and the gates read the changesets, so this is a body edit for the seat (③), not a verdict item. The plugin-side `WriteWallRowVerdict` twin (security-plugin.ts:329) follows the file's `WriteImageCheckSeam` precedent (the engine is a devDependency) and is welded by the two cross-package pins.

### ② Semver level

Both changesets grade `patch` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the kind alone — a `none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (header: a declared `none` must grade every entry it introduces `patch`) runs in the `Check Changeset` job, which is `success` on this head. The ruling's execution line set the level "per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3"; the dispatch and claim's `minor` was the dispatch's own word, not the ruling's, and the dev declared the deviation. `patch` is right. Both touched packages publish (neither `package.json` is private) and each carries its changeset; the changeset bodies match what the diff publishes (the objectql one names the member, both types, the refusal shape, the unregistered state and the hook limit; the plugin-security one names the one-spelling extraction, `writeWallVerdict`, its `null` exits and the start-time warning). No `content/docs/releases/` or `CHANGELOG.md` edit.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Probe docblock (report 6336244213, ruling's execution line): CLOSED in this PR.** The `registerWriteGateProbe` docblock now says step 3.7 is asked as the scope pre-test with no row and answers `true` for a payload naming a refused organization; the `canWriteObject` arm-10 docblock says the same. The probe's body is byte-identical to base.
2. **Changeset level `patch` (dev deviation 1): RIGHT**, judged under ②.
3. **`field` on the dry run but not the commit (Acceptance note 3): ACCEPTED as pre-existing shape.** `import-runner.ts` builds a dry-run row from `verdict.errors[0]` (`field`, `code`, composed `error`), while a committed row's failure is built from the thrown error, which carries `code` and `status` and no field. The REST pin compares `ok`, `action`, `code`, `error`, `droppedFields` on both doors and pins `field: organization_id` on the dry run alone. `_record` is the contract's own sentinel (`ValidateDataIssueSchema.field`: "`_record` for an object-level rule"; `rule-validator.ts` uses it), and ruling item 2 prescribes it.
4. **Named limit (hook-written organization): KEPT**, in the `validate()` docblock as ruling item 4 asks.
5. **`null` exits (Acceptance note 5): ANSWERED in ①(b).** Observation for the seat, not a verdict item: `writeWallVerdict`'s `catch { return null }` around `resolveOperationPrincipals` (security-plugin.ts:8727–8731) does not discriminate the refusal it expects (`PermissionDeniedError`, `GuestOrganizationUnresolvedError`) from a fault — a store error inside `resolveDelegatorContext` would also fall to "wall not asked" and return the preview to its blind state with no log line (the permission-subsystem failure is logged at `error` inside the prologue; a delegator read fault is not). The write stays fail-closed on every such caller, so this cannot admit anything; it is a loudness question ("Absence must be loud") for a follow-up card or a dismissal, the seat's call.
6. **File surface beyond the claim (dev deviation 2): ACCEPTED, both rows are what their gates ask.** (i) `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 6c, checked sentence by sentence against the code: `writeWallVerdict` returns `null` on `isSystem` (:8724) — true; the preview then treats the rows as with nothing registered — true (`wallVerdicts` null, every `wallRefusals[i]` undefined); "the elevated preview's `readonly` strips stay skipped as they always were" — true, the strips sit under `if (!options?.context?.isSystem)` (engine.ts:15918), unchanged; "the whole security middleware short-circuits before step 3.7" — true (:2542); "Lose: nothing the write enforces" — true. Its gate `check-system-context-census` runs in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`: `success`. (ii) The READERS row in `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` for the module-scope `organization_id` literal in the new verdict type, disposition `not-a-read`: the literal is a type member, the engine reads no row through it; its gate is the objectql suite under `Test Core`, in progress at this reading.
7. **Deviation 3 (the second ask): ANSWERED in ①(d).** Inside the ruling, right, pinned.
8. **Pins and ablation named by the ruling: PRESENT.** The two cells with controls (organizations pin, 10 cases; `security: false` is the nothing-registered control), the equivalence pin in the shape of `can-write-object-admission.test.ts` (21 cases, the real middleware through `executeWithMiddleware` against the seam, equal admit / refuse / code / message / `judgesOrganization`), the HTTP door (M5a, M5b, a mixed batch, the `single` control), the engine contract (14). The ablation is reported one-off with the ruling's shape (feature-detect renamed in `dist`, organizations 7 red / 3 green, rest 3 red / 1 green, every failure an assertion) — a reading of the dev's, not re-run here.
9. **Cross-lane declaration to #21118 (comment 6339470244):** asserted in the claim and the PR body; that comment is outside this review's input set and is not read here.
10. **PR form:** draft, base `main`, body opens on `Fixes #25062` after the attribution comment — the PR delivers the whole of ruling A, so closing the card on merge is right. `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`: `success`.
